podcast.title: Album Release Significance
podcast.body: Imperial Records' decision to release Fats Domino's first album, "Rock and Rollin' with Fat Domino," after six years of exclusively recording singles, was highly significant. It signaled a shift from sales primarily to jukebox manufacturers to direct consumer purchases, particularly by a new white audience willing to buy LPs, a rarity for R&B artists in the 1950s. "Imperial records actually put out an album by him rather than just singles for the first time in the six years he'd been recording for them."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Dave Bartholomew's A&R Role
podcast.body: Dave Bartholomew worked as an A&R man for Imperial Records after his military service, a role through which he would eventually suggest signing Fats Domino. "he got work as an A&R man for Imperial Records."

podcast.title: Label for Ricky Nelson
podcast.body: Imperial Records was the label for teen idol Ricky Nelson, who needed material, leading to Johnny and Dorsey Burnette's successful songwriting partnership for him. "Imperial Records, who had a new teen idol star who needed material."

podcast.title: Release of "Wasted Days and Wasted Nights"
podcast.body: Imperial Records released Freddie Fender's "Wasted Days and Wasted Nights" in 1959, giving it some initial traction before his arrest for marijuana possession halted its progress. "It was released again on a bigger label, Imperial."
